parsed.explanation: The operative regime is one of recurring, documented police targeting of queer gatherings: mass 2017 raids with beatings, forced medical examinations, electric shocks, rape threats, blackmail and dozens imprisoned or fined, repeated in a July 2023 private-party raid with forced exams and sexual harassment; a March 2024 trans murder went inadequately investigated. No anti-discrimination law, no marker change, media 77% hateful and state-channel hate speech. Countervailing: no documented border/document screening layer, no execution or capital charge for gender expression, a 2024 regional-court ruling and 2019 government acknowledgement (no shown operative domestic remedy), and functioning civil society. Raids are severe but not universal-exposure to every visitor; the traveller's main exposure is venue/gathering policing and impunity after violence.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No sourced material addresses entry, visa, marker checks or airport screening practice for trans travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor carries a home-issued passport; no documented interaction with domestic marker rules at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: 2017 raids detained 100+, with beatings, forced medical examinations, electric shocks, rape threats, blackmail; 60+ imprisoned or fined. July 2023 party raid with forced exams and sexual harassment. Threats of outing.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None shown operating; 2019 acknowledgement and April 2024 regional-court ruling produced no demonstrated domestic remedy or accountability.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Policing of venues, parties and street presence is the pathway from routine presence to custody mistreatment.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Custodial mistreatment documented in police detention; prison placement by gender not documented. State-affiliated television aired anti-LGBTI hate speech in 2024.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State media framing feeds officer discretion in enforcement and investigation.

care_services.exposure: March demanding trans healthcare access met with state-media hate speech; forced medical examinations by police documented. Routine visitor care access not documented.
care_services.interaction: Health settings are also sites of forced examination during raids.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: raids presented as anti-prostitution action; 77% of 428 media pieces (2023) hateful or biased; officials use discriminatory language; activist ordered to remove rainbow flag.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented; no SOGI anti-discrimination prohibition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing legitimises police raids and discourages reporting.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented: 18-year-old forcibly transported by family after coming out; 14-year-old died after school homophobic bullying with no staff action. A minor travelling with a guardian may face family/community outing pressure.
minors_guardians.protection: After the 2019 death: staff dismissed, principal sentenced, national anti-bullying plan and hotline; a narrow, education-specific remedy.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family and school authority can override a minor's autonomy; police rarely involved protectively.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: March 2024 murder of a trans woman in the capital with an inadequate police investigation. No rate, denominator or baseline comparison given.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; impunity indicated by the inadequate investigation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of hate-crime law and hostile media reduce reporting and response.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies pursued abroad; accountability sought outside the country; domestic recourse largely absent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: April 2024 regional human-rights court ruling and 2019 government acknowledgement; press council exists but its handling of anti-LGBTI media is unassessed.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: International rulings have not visibly changed policing practice, as the 2023 raid shows.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: 0.15-A shows routine arrest for presentation, months of pretrial beatings, compelled confessions and a capital provision with courts deferring to security services. Here capital charging/execution is undocumented and arrests follow raids/gatherings rather than universal presentation checks, though custody torture and impunity are comparable.

Similar but harsher: 0.25-C has birth-sex prison housing and cross-dressing prosecutions with brief sentences and no capital cases. This dossier adds documented torture in raids, sexual harassment, recurring party raids and an uninvestigated murder, placing it lower than 0.25-C despite the absence of a facility-specific statute.

Materially worse: 0.35-A is exclusion, seizure and humiliation at the border with no imprisonment. Here detention involves beatings, forced medical examinations, extortion and imprisonment, and violence against trans people goes unpunished, so severity is a tier or more above.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is weak rule-of-law enforcement turned against queer people: police raid private gatherings with documented torture-adjacent mistreatment and imprisonment, media and state channels supply threat-framing, no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse exists, and the one recorded trans murder drew an inadequate investigation. Offsetting elements are limited and mostly non-operative for a visitor: no documented border or document-screening layer, no capital charge tied to gender expression, a regional-court ruling and 2019 acknowledgement without demonstrated domestic effect, and a functioning civil society concentrated in the capital. Because the raids are episodic rather than a universal-exposure checkpoint regime, and execution is undocumented, the case sits near, but above, the catastrophic floor.
